title: Module quiz: The agentic loop, in depth

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team's runs often end with the status `max_turns` because one tool keeps failing, and raising the cap from ten to forty only made each failed run cost four times as much. What should they do?

options.text: Turn the cap off entirely and let the model decide when a failure is final
options.says: Ruled out because a run needs a backstop: "A count is added so that a run that does not converge is stopped."

options.text: Raise the cap again and again until the failures stop ending in the cap itself
options.says: Ruled out because the count is not what is wrong: "The status is a signal to read the conversation, which the practice keeps whole for that reason."

options.text: Read the saved conversation, then repair that helper's description
options.says: The status is a signal about a run that does not converge, and the conversation shows why.
Ruled out because the count "has its own status", and reporting `done` for it hides the problem that the fixed loop also hides.

origin.section: Anti-pattern two: the count as the loop

questions.stem: A loop that follows this module's practice receives a reply whose stop reason asks for a tool, but its content holds only a sentence of text. What should it do?

options.text: Send an empty user message and call the model once more to see what it does
options.says: Ruled out because the API does not accept it: "an empty message, which a loop can send by accident when a `tool_use` reply holds no call, is refused."

options.text: Finish with a malformed status and make no further call
options.says: There is nothing to answer, and the practice stops with its own status.

options.text: Return the sentence to the user as the finished answer
options.says: Ruled out because narration is not an answer: "Only the reply that ends the turn holds the answer."

options.text: Call the model again with the same messages and hope for a call
options.says: Ruled out because guessing is what the loop avoids: "A value the loop has never seen must not be guessed at."

origin.section: What the loop owns when you write it yourself

questions.stem: A dashboard alerts on every run that ends with a null stop reason and zero cost, and the team suspects a parsing bug. What explains those runs?

options.text: A turn limit, which can report a zero cost for the unfinished run of the agent
options.says: Ruled out because a run that the loop ends has a value: "`stop_reason` carries the value from the last assistant response before the loop ended".

options.text: A refusal by the model, which is reported with a null stop reason at first sight
options.says: Ruled out because a refusal sets the reason: "Claude declined to respond."

options.text: A normal run that has no stop reason to give
options.says: Ruled out because a normal end carries a value: "Claude finished its response naturally."

options.text: A crashed session, which closes in an error result whose figures may be blanked
options.says: The documentation describes this result for a crash: "the final result is an `error_during_execution` whose cost fields may be zeroed and whose `stop_reason` is `null`".

origin.section: What the Agent SDK does in that position
